slides.heading: System Design Interviews
slides.subtitle: Framework and back-of-envelope maths
slides.narration: Welcome to the SystemsExpert series. Before the individual designs, here's the framework to run every system design interview, and the numbers you should know for quick estimates.

slides.heading: The 45-minute framework
bullets: Clarify the scope and the users.
slides.narration: Run every interview in the same order. Step 1: Clarify the scope and the users. Step 2: Functional and non-functional requirements. Step 3: Rough estimates. Step 4: Entities and API. Step 5: High-level diagram. Step 6: Deep dives on bottlenecks. Step 7: Trade-offs and failure modes. Keep the interviewer involved at every step.

slides.heading: Back-of-envelope numbers
bullets: 1 day ≈ 86,400 s ≈ 10^5 s; 1M requests/day ≈ 12 QPS; peak ≈ 2–3× the average.
Character 1 B; tweet-size text ~300 B; photo ~200 KB–2 MB; 1 min of HD video ~50–100 MB.
One server handles ~10k concurrent connections and ~1k–10k simple QPS; Redis does ~100k ops/s.
A disk sequential read is ~100× faster than random; reading 1 MB from memory takes ~250 µs, from SSD ~1 ms.

slides.heading: Recap
slides.narration: To recap: use the same structure every time, settle requirements before drawing boxes, let estimates size the design, and always finish with trade-offs and failure modes. Next, the fundamentals, in four parts.
